label: clean
rationale: 0 of 128 graded scenarios failed, so there is no failure to attribute and `clean` is the only label the schema permits; every FAILURE_ATTRIBUTING label is refused on a trial that failed nothing. Recorded rather than left absent so a read trial is distinguishable from an unread one. The point worth writing down is that this clean pass is INFORMATIVE, which a clean pass is not automatically: challenge/starter/subject.mjs is a refuse-everything stub (`const allowed = false` with a `// TODO: decide against the policy in SPEC.md`), and challenge/README.md states "Refusing everything fails" because blocking the attack is worth nothing if the approved payment never goes out - so the shipped starter fails by construction and the package does not contain the answer. This is the opposite of the access-token and delegated-wallet packages, whose starters were complete passing solutions and whose clean passes therefore carry no information. challenge/SPEC.md is self-contained and normative (eight ordered rules with their reason codes, an exhaustive legal-transition list), and this submission independently implements all eight P-codes in the specified order in 231 lines, allowing permitted calls and blocking forbidden ones. Not difficulty evidence under any label, but a real saturation result for this family.
